My guest this week is Michael Movison, the head of Consilient Research at Counterpoint Global.
Michael is an all-time favorite guest here on the show, and this is his fourth appearance.
We discussed one of the biggest topics in the world of investing, the shift from public to
private markets that has taken place over the last several decades.
We explore the reasons for this shift, the biggest overall changes in capital markets, and what the future may hold.
Along the way, we explore other fascinating topics like the rise of intangible asset investment, employee-based compensation as a form of financing and more.
If you enjoy this conversation, I urge you to read Michael's paper on the topic, which will be linked in the show notes.
Please enjoy this great conversation with Michael Movison.
Okay, Michael, for the first in-person podcast that I've done since early March, this is great.
Great to see you, as always.
The topic of our conversation is your latest paper on the transition from public to private equity, which is effectively a book that you wrote.
And one thing that we've been talking about for several years just between you and I and I know you've been thinking about forever.
I think your motivation would be an interesting place to start.
Why take so much time and effort to write a mini book on this key transition?
So there are a couple things, Patrick.
First of all, great to be with you and great to be with you in person.
The first was in 2016, we wrote a piece about, we called it the incredibly shrinking universe of companies.
There have been some academic work on this idea called the listing gap, which

2016, so it was 20 years up because of the peak year for a number of public companies was

it's obviously multiples of the venture capital industry. And even in venture, if you look
